# Ecosystem Field Guide: Design Questions in Practice

This guide is organized by decisions, not package inventory. Each exhibit is
public and reader-verifiable, and each is evidence for a bounded design claim
rather than a recommendation to copy a package wholesale.

## How can one declaration serve several consumers?

### rtemis: property contracts as inspectable data

[rtemis](https://github.com/rtemis-org/rtemis) treats a property declaration
as more than a validator closure. Its public
[`PropertySpec` implementation](https://github.com/rtemis-org/rtemis/blob/f60ac02b32f58373a2ba7f965b9c1c450dd2200a/R/010_Props.R)
retains value type, container shape, bounds, choices, defaults, null behavior,
tuning intent, conditional applicability, and data-dependent bounds as data.
That choice is causal: once the declaration can be inspected, the package can
use the same facts to build executable S7 properties, establish defaults,
project schemas and interfaces, and prepare a configuration against training
data. A closure alone could enforce a value locally, but it could not explain
the rule to those other consumers.

The distinction between a value and a candidate set shows why the extra model
matters. Shape is not enough: a length-two vector might be one value, a range,
or a search space. By recording tuning intent independently, `PropertySpec`
prevents downstream code from reverse-engineering semantics from shape.
Similarly, a data-dependent bound remains declared with the property even
though it cannot be resolved until the training data supplies the missing
context. Declaration and enforcement can therefore happen at different
times without becoming different rules.

This concentration of knowledge creates obligations. A default should satisfy
its own declaration; incompatible metadata axes should fail when the property
is defined; and generated validators, schemas, and interfaces need alignment
tests. Contract-as-data removes independently maintained definitions, not the
possibility of a faulty projection. Nor does it make every rule reversible:
reconstruction is credible only for the vocabulary that the declaration
actually records.

**Decision test.** Use contract-as-data when several real consumers need the
same facts and their agreement can be tested. A handwritten
`S7::new_property()` remains simpler when construction is the only consumer.

## Which objects are values, snapshots, or runtime owners?

### deputy: portable definitions at a permission boundary

[deputy](https://github.com/JamesHWade/deputy) runs tasks with an
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) chat and R tools. Its
[public documentation](https://jameshwade.github.io/deputy/articles/runtime-integration.html)
separates declarative configuration from a live run: tool definitions,
permission policies, and usage limits describe requested behavior, while the
`Agent` owns execution, streaming, counters, and host interaction.
`AgentResult` records how a completed run ended, including stop reason and
usage information.

The split follows ownership. Definitions and policies can travel as data
because they do not themselves contain a live model connection or grant a
capability. At execution time, the host binds symbolic tools and applies its
permission policy; valid configuration is therefore not confused with
authority. The running agent needs identity because it coordinates changing
state and effects, while its completed result can become a value-like fact.
Deputy also composes with ellmer's public tool and structured-output meanings
instead of inventing parallel ones, keeping package policy at the layer that
owns it.

Read-only result fields, where used, express the lifecycle of completed facts.
They are not evidence that every S7 value should be read-only. Editable
configuration can retain value semantics and invariant-preserving replacement.

**Decision test.** Choose a reference owner for shared identity, live
resources, or an observable lifecycle. Use values for portable definitions
and completed facts, and keep requested capability distinct from host-granted
authority.

## When is a semantic middle representation worth its cost?

### sqlr: one model for rendering, reflection, and comparison

[sqlr](https://github.com/nbenn/sqlr) supplies a representation of a database
schema that is neither SQL text nor a live connection. Constructors create
that model; dialect objects render it; `sqlr_reflect()` reconstructs it from a
catalog; and `sqlr_equal()` and `sqlr_diff()` compare its meaning. These are
independent consumers, so the schema model prevents each operation from
re-parsing text or inventing a private account of tables and constraints.

The model also makes policy visible. Rendering can order tables by dependency
and defer cycle-closing foreign keys to later statements. Dialects carry
engine-specific behavior without requiring a live connection, and the package
deliberately declines to offer an untested “ANSI SQL” fallback. Reflection is
bounded by what a database exposes, so missing catalog facts remain documented
limits instead of guessed values. Comparison can then ignore incidental
constraint order or generated names and report differences in domain terms.

The resulting round-trip law is semantic, not textual:
rendering into a particular engine and reflecting back should preserve the
modeled meaning that engine can represent. Exact representation, canonical
form, and domain equality remain separate claims. The
[public generic definitions at revision `8325581`](https://github.com/nbenn/sqlr/blob/8325581ad859b408408738dcc289bcad05360d58/R/generics.R)
make that operation vocabulary inspectable.

### Additional exhibit: quickr's typed compiler IR

[quickr](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/quickr) gives an IR a different
reason to exist. Its R-to-Fortran compiler reads an in-language type
declaration, lowers source through typed objects, and passes those objects
between analysis and code-generation stages; the public
[`quick.R` source](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/quickr/blob/edd403766e612ef4867ad817ead3dc366dc15d77/R/quick.R)
shows compiled artifacts such as `FortranSubroutine` being consumed as
structured values. A typed IR is justified here because translation and
analysis are the product. For a single textual rewrite, the same class graph
would be ceremony.

**Decision test.** Introduce an intermediate representation after at least two
consumers need the same stable meaning. Rendering alone may need an adapter;
rendering plus reflection and comparison, or analysis plus code generation,
can justify a shared typed model.

## Who owns the contract: S7 properties or an external schema?

### S7schema: an externally validated container

[S7schema](https://cran.r-project.org/package=S7schema) validates YAML
configuration against JSON Schema using AJV through V8. S7 classes supply the
surrounding configuration and extension machinery, while detailed domain
entries remain list content whose contract belongs to the external schema.
This avoids translating every foreign rule into a second property system and
keeps conformance with the authority that other implementations can share.

The cost is a wider gap between manipulation and certification. Arbitrary list
editing does not automatically preserve validity, so an API must say which
boundaries revalidate and which operations merely rearrange content. External
authority removes duplicate rules only if consumers continue to consult it.

### stacbuildr: native boundary constructors plus conformance

[stacbuildr](https://stevenpawley.r-universe.dev/stacbuildr) makes the other
trade-off. It gives STAC catalogs, collections, and items native classes,
projects them into familiar tabular or spatial forms, and validates emitted
documents against published STAC schemas. Its `item_from_terra()`,
`item_from_sf()`, and `item_from_lidr()` constructors translate objects users
already hold while extracting spatial metadata. The native layer is useful
because R-side construction, navigation, and projection need nominal
concepts; the external validator remains useful because STAC, not the R
package, owns wire conformance.

The contrast is not “schema versus classes.” S7schema keeps detailed entries
under external-schema authority because the container and extension machinery
are the main R-side concern. stacbuildr adds a semantic layer because its major
nodes have operations in R, but still refuses to make that layer the sole
judge of an external specification. In both designs, authority follows the
knowledge rather than the implementation language.

### Additional exhibit: typedjson's minimal annotations

[typedjson](https://github.com/nbenn/typedjson) addresses a narrower authority
problem: JSON cannot express every distinction among R values. Its
[public design at revision `7160c06`](https://github.com/nbenn/typedjson/blob/7160c060e260bec3d284c39e51a9a5331779aa14/README.md)
keeps ordinary values as ordinary JSON and adds annotations only where the
wire format would otherwise lose information. Ordinary numeric spellings can
preserve integer versus double (`1` versus `1.0`); annotations carry
distinctions such as typed missing or empty values, non-finite numbers,
attributes, and object-system metadata. The round-trip goal determines the
annotations; it
does not justify turning the whole document into an opaque serialization
envelope. This is a useful minimum-metadata rule whenever readability and
fidelity compete.

**Decision test.** Ask whether downstream operations need nominal identity and
invariants inside R. If not, a validated external-schema container may
suffice. If they do, add a semantic layer while retaining the external
conformance oracle. Annotate a wire form only for distinctions its native
vocabulary cannot preserve.

## Should failure be a condition or a value?

### resultr: explicit outcome sequencing

[resultr](https://github.com/TransGirlCodes/resultr) defines an abstract
`Result` parent with `Success` and `Failure` variants. Its
[`Result.R` implementation](https://github.com/TransGirlCodes/resultr/blob/0f53d4ee03138cc93a3feef4900746f672d12fe8/R/Result.R)
provides inspection, unwrapping, defaults, and `and_then()`. A `Success`
applies the next computation; a `Failure` returns itself, making
short-circuiting part of the protocol rather than a convention repeated by
each caller.

The same source makes the condition/value boundary explicit.
`wrap_in_result()` maps ordinary values to `Success`, errors and warnings to
`Failure`, and existing results to themselves; `and_then()` uses
`rlang::try_fetch()` at that boundary. This adapter matters because R
conditions and result values serve different traffic. Conditions support
immediate non-local control flow. Outcome values can be stored, inspected,
combined, or returned through an ordinary value channel.

The exhibit therefore supports a choice, not a universal replacement for
conditions. Programmer errors and failures requiring immediate unwinding
still belong in the condition channel. A result protocol must also say
whether failures short-circuit or accumulate; resultr demonstrates the former,
while validation systems often need the latter.

**Decision test.** Choose the channel per subsystem, then define one deliberate
adapter. Do not alternate ad hoc between thrown conditions and returned
failures.

## How much behavior belongs in a reusable contract?

### Additional exhibit: s7contract's executable laws

[s7contract](https://github.com/sounkou-bioinfo/s7contract) separates several
strengths of agreement. Its
[public README at revision `41dce50`](https://github.com/sounkou-bioinfo/s7contract/blob/41dce50d482ad4bfac382e859662abcae0ba56c4/README.md)
describes structural interfaces as named sets of required generics, explicit
traits with registration and defaults, runtime argument and return checks,
and generative laws with generators and shrinking. Method availability can
show that an object has the required vocabulary; executable laws probe whether
implementations preserve behavioral promises that a dispatch table cannot
express.

The causal lesson is that “implements” has layers. Structural conformance is
cheap and queryable, runtime contracts can localize bad inputs or outputs, and
generative laws can be reused by third-party implementations. None supplies a
compile-time proof, and sampled laws do not establish a theorem. Their value
is to turn otherwise prose-only obligations into public, repeatable tests.

**Decision test.** Add reusable conformance laws when independent
implementations share behavior important enough to test. Do not mistake
method presence or generated examples for proof of all valid inputs.

## When should policy become a composable object?

### Additional exhibit: optimizers7 and parameters7

[optimizers7](https://github.com/statmodels7/optimizers7) and
[parameters7](https://github.com/statmodels7/parameters7) extract mathematical
policies that modeling packages often bury inside loops and parameterizations.
The public
[optimizers7 design](https://github.com/statmodels7/optimizers7/blob/c50e41416c411b530124f2329679cdc72ec85ff0/README.md)
models an optimizer separately from its stopping rule. Because “finished” is
an independent policy, users can compose or replace stopping criteria without
forking the algorithm. The
[parameters7 design](https://github.com/statmodels7/parameters7/blob/21076ad92cd2442b8be767d1b0546f7f783937c5/README.md)
models constrained parameters as reusable maps with inverses and derivatives,
so an optimizer or likelihood can depend on a stable mathematical interface
instead of one package's private encoding.

This decomposition pays when behavior varies independently and has operations
of its own. A tolerance used by exactly one loop may remain an argument. A
stopping rule that combines criteria, or a parameter map that must be
evaluated, inverted, and differentiated, has earned nominal identity and
dispatch. Both packages also keep their abstractions narrow: optimization
need not know what an observation is, and a parameter map need not own a
statistical model.

**Decision test.** Promote policy to an object when it varies independently,
composes with peers, or supports a reusable operation vocabulary. Keep a
scalar option as data when no consumer needs those capabilities.

## Cross-case synthesis

Across these cases, S7 is valuable less as a syntax for records than as a way
to put authority and variation in inspectable places. rtemis centralizes facts
because several projections need them. sqlr and quickr introduce middle
representations because several transformations share stable semantics.
S7schema and stacbuildr keep external specifications authoritative even when
R-side objects add ergonomics. resultr names a control protocol, s7contract
names conformance obligations, and optimizers7 makes an independently varying
policy composable.

The recurring limit is equally important. Central metadata needs projection
tests; an IR needs multiple substantive consumers; a native document model
does not supersede its wire specification; a result value does not replace
all conditions; generated laws are evidence rather than proof; and a policy
object must earn its indirection. These are not package-specific cautions.
They are the costs created by the same design moves that provide the benefit.

## Questions to carry into a design

- How many consumers need the same declared knowledge?
- Is this object a portable value, completed snapshot, or live owner?
- Does a middle representation have more than one substantive consumer?
- Is contract authority local, external, or shared through tested projections?
- What equality relation makes a round trip meaningful?
- Does failure control execution immediately, or travel as data?
- Is a behavior merely configurable, or independently composable?
- Which unknown content is rejected, preserved inertly, or interpreted?

S7 earns its place when nominal meaning, invariant placement, or generic
operations simplify consumers—not merely because structured data exists.
